clue.text: Extra job for doctor on dismounting

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a standard abbreviation for a doctor
taken as written
to light (or alight) is to get down from a horse, so dismounting is lighting

explanation.surface: A doctor takes on a second job while getting off his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighting' here is the old verb to light, to come down from a horse or carriage, not illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlighting is taking secret paid work in addition to a regular post, so it is a second, extra job.

clue.text: One who accepts aims of corrupt circle

definitions.text: One who accepts aims of corrupt circle

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters of aims of are spoilt and need rearranging

parts.note: a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A member who signs up to the goals of a crooked ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges AIMS OF, then O (circle) is added; the whole clue also describes a gang member.
explanation.definitionFit: A mafioso is a member of the Mafia, a criminal organisation, and so shares its corrupt goals.

clue.text: Maintaining advantage, unlike previous clue

explanation.surface: A note that this clue keeps the edge, unlike the one before.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous clue is 1 Down, read as 'one down'; this one is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one-up is having a lead over a rival; the opposite direction to 'one down' names the clue before it.

clue.text: Nothing's right for Romeo and Juliet, say

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and the 's adds an S
a Tory is a member of the right-wing Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A claim that nothing suits the doomed young lovers of Verona.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet is given as an example, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about two young lovers is a classic romantic tale.

clue.text: Soldier both sides miss

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the two sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A soldier misses both flanks of the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb about missing a target but is a noun, a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title and term for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: They saw us rip ends off reference books

indicators.note: ends off removes the final letter of each of the four words They, saw, us, rip

explanation.surface: Readers claim that we were spotted tearing pages from the dictionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of each word leaves THE SA U RI, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of synonyms, a standard reference work; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Depression in corporation

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a big belly, and the depression is the hollow in its middle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a company in a slump, but it is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is the small hollow in the middle of the stomach.

clue.text: Flower is put in water I changed

indicators.note: put in places the word is inside the other letters
changed says the letters of water and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener adds an ingredient to the water to alter the bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' could suggest a river, but here it is a plant; 'changed' rearranges the letters of the watery word with I before the other piece goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing plant with hanging clusters of lilac blooms.

clue.text: Be disparaging about second spot

indicators.note: about says the word for disparaging goes around the other piece

parts.note: to decry is to speak of something with disparagement

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the runner-up position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a place, but it is the verb to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to catch sight of something at a distance, to notice it.

clue.text: Work of undisciplined linesman upsets severe ref

indicators.note: upsets says the letters of severe and ref are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A football linesman, angry with a harsh referee, overturns his decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The linesman is a poet writing lines, undisciplined because free verse ignores metre and rhyme; 'upsets' rearranges SEVERE REF.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, the output of a poet who refuses formal discipline.

clue.text: Concealing nothing, in place of spokesman

indicators.note: Concealing tells us that one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: vice, as in vice-captain, means in place of
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A spokesman who hides nothing while standing in for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: VICE (Latin for 'in place of') conceals O to give V-O-ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice can be a person who speaks for a group, its mouthpiece or representative.

clue.text: Face puzzle after work

indicators.note: after puts the word for puzzle behind the word for work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work of music
to pose is to puzzle or baffle, as in posing a problem

explanation.surface: Facing a brainteaser once the working day is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to stand against them, to resist.

clue.text: In the sea, the French like dancing

indicators.note: In places the French article inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: French people swimming in the sea seem to enjoy dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletic describes movement graceful in the manner of ballet, the dance form.

clue.text: Bloody awful pupil? No longer

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of Bloody are in a terrible state and must be reordered

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a dreadful schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody awful' reads as one British expletive phrase, but 'awful' rearranges BLOODY. An old boy is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An old boy is a former student of a school, someone who was a pupil there once.

clue.text: Argument could be appealing, so to speak

definitions.text: could be appealing, so to speak

explanation.surface: A row might turn out attractive, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appealing, so to speak' is to be heard as 'a pealing', the sound of church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is British slang for a heated quarrel, and also the sound of a ringing bell.

clue.text: Quality seen on stage

explanation.surface: A remark about the calibre of what an audience sees.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a stage property, an object used by actors, usually shortened to 'prop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a characteristic or attribute, and also any portable item used in a theatre production.

clue.text: Hero, for one, that's good man in crowd

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations for that is and saint inside the word for crowd

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng of people
IE, from id est, means that is
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A heroic person is described as a decent fellow in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero here is the figure of Greek legend, a priestess of Aphrodite loved by Leander, not a brave person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hero served in the temple of Aphrodite at Sestos as a female cleric.

clue.text: Repaired siren with instrument outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for instrument wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a reed is a reed instrument, such as an oboe
a siren is a seductive woman, a vamp

explanation.surface: A warning siren fixed with a musical instrument on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siren' suggests an alarm, but it is a temptress, a vamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or patch up into improved shape.

clue.text: Convenient pieces for versatile workers

parts.note: handy means close by and convenient
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Useful bits of kit for people who can turn their hand to anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Handymen are odd-job workers who can do many kinds of repairs around a house.

clue.text: Springtime for university girl

explanation.surface: A young woman's spring at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name of the spring term at Oxford and some other universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford term from January to Easter bears this name, which is also a female first name.

clue.text: Win confidence of underworld power

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
an arm is a branch of power, as in the arm of the law

explanation.surface: Gaining the trust of a powerful gangland figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangsters, but it is the classical realm of the dead, ruled by Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to charm away their suspicion or hostility, winning their trust.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, outwardly crazy? Fool

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for crazy sits on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: mad means crazy
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: Is a man who seems mad on the outside really a fool?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to deceive them, leading them astray.

clue.text: Lost, dear? Switch central quarters for guide

indicators.note: split the eight letters of Lost dear into four pairs and swap the middle two pairs

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lost loved one to change direction and find the way.
explanation.walkthrough: LOSTDEAR splits into LO-ST-DE-AR; swapping the second and third pairs gives LO-DE-ST-AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, such as the Pole Star, hence any guiding principle.

clue.text: Authority remains silent

parts.note: keeping quiet means saying nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: Those in charge refuse to comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains silent' is read as 'says O', with O as nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authority to act.

clue.text: Limousines sought by film stars?

parts.note: big American automobiles are limousines, and the phrase as heard also suggests the Academy Awards that film stars covet

explanation.surface: Movie celebrities hunting for luxury cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Limousines are typically American cars; said aloud, the answer is close to the Oscars that film stars seek.
explanation.definitionFit: Limousines are large luxury automobiles of the kind made in America.

clue.text: Vessel carrying vital supplies, from China or Taiwan

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words China or Taiwan

explanation.surface: A ship bringing essential cargo from East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel carrying oxygenated blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, taking oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.

clue.text: Does increase herd when they do this

definitions.text: Does increase herd when they do this

parts.words: Does increase herd when they do this
parts.note: does are female deer, and they enlarge the herd by giving birth to young

explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb, but it is the plural of doe, a female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn, said of a deer, is to give birth to a young one.

clue.text: Lustful extremes of ribaldry

explanation.surface: Bawdy talk at its most outrageous is lewd.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read literally: the extremes of the word ribaldry are 'R and Y', and writing that phrase out in full, conjunction included, gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lecherous; the ribaldry phrase names its first and last letters joined by a conjunction.

clue.text: Even old actor leaves producer in city

parts.note: to plane a surface is to make it even or level
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Even a veteran actor walks out on the theatre producer in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb (the actor walks out) but is a noun: foliage grown by a tree common on city streets, such as London's.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is the classic urban street tree, producing broad foliage in towns.

clue.text: Stop, as one must at bridge

explanation.surface: Advice to pause, like a card player who must keep their cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, each player holds a hand of thirteen cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from acting is to delay or stop; a bridge player must also keep a set of cards in the fist.
